summary: The run's remaining time went to source verification and it turned up two real defects in my own record, both now fixed. First, re-reading the snapshot path showed that one clause of my repair Fact was over-broad: a leader does send a snapshot when it cannot fetch the follower's previous entry (replication.go 222-224), and a leader-side user restore deliberately leaves a hole above such a follower's next index (raft.go 1097-1199), so a node with a complete log can be reached this way; the Fact now claims only that none of the four paths is triggered by the node's own restart in the observed scenarios and states the exception. Second, inspecting the applied revision showed a merge artifact: that Fact's conditions had been overwritten with the trigger Fact's conditions, two source anchors had gone missing, and the receipt for the in-protocol repair had dropped out. This revision restores the repair-scope conditions, the full source list (bootstrap refusal, RecoverCluster, snapshot trigger, user-restore hole), and all four receipts, with a changed_premise that names the artifact explicitly rather than editing silently. The statement, the interpretation's caveat and every other record are unchanged, and the submission validates.
